subject.declared_domain: NFRA_CSE.P3 -- the graph_head PRODUCER: materialize the live CloudNode/CloudEdge graph as GRAPH_HEAD CSEs into the C0 log. Declared as 'the persistent full-graph stream that becomes the log's SUBSTANTIVE content at 0.3'. Implements contract_graph_head (ProducerKind.GRAPH_HEAD, ref = the Nessie marker at emission, compiler graph-head-delta-compiler, recognizers cloudnode/cloudedge_graph_recognizer, subject via map_cloudnode / CLOUDEDGE_TO_RELATIONSHIP, verb = create per the HEAD state). Declared SELF-CONTAINED and in-VPC only.

as_of.graph_vintage: This is a LIVE producer, unlike the first two on this face. globgrph.cse source=graph_head holds 44 partitions / 86,607 rows spanning event_date 2026-07-08..2026-08-30, the newest written 2026-08-30. Read in full: all 44 partitions synced and every row counted.

methodology.how: build_graph_head_cses (:159-187) scans graph_nodes for (node_id, node_type) and graph_edges for (src_id, dst_id, edge_type) through a pyiceberg catalog, then recognizes each: node_cse (:99-120) maps node_type -> Entity via cs.map_cloudnode, honest-degrading to Concept(untyped)+0.2 on a map gap; edge_cse (:122-152) maps edge_type -> Relationship via cs.map_cloudedge resolved BY THE DST NODE TYPE, returns None for an unmapped edge_type, and independently degrades the src subject. Nodes and edges are each sliced by an optional limit. main (:190-222) then validates fail-closed and appends. THE PRODUCTION PATH IS NOT main() -- see cadence.

composes.note: scanned for node_id + node_type; also builds the node_type map used to resolve BOTH endpoints of every edge
scanned for src_id, dst_id, edge_type -- the RAW edge axis, deliberately not comp-kuzu's projected graph

map_cloudnode and map_cloudedge are the certed maps; a gap in either is what produces the untyped degrade, so the 37% untyped share measured below is a property of THAT module, not of this one. map_cloudedge is target-typed for the polysemous OWNED_BY (verified at cse_schema.py:399-403), and the same module ships owned_by_object_census (:406-413) for the unknown-object-type hazard -- which this producer does not call
get_catalog, validate_batch, append_cses, ensure_cse_table, stamp_marker, and NESSIE_URI
leg_graphhead (:146-160) is the ACTUAL production caller -- it imports this module and calls build_graph_head_cses directly, bypassing main()

cadence.declared_rhythm: The module's own CLI declares --limit N as 'the default first-proof mode', --full for 'the substantive-content run', and --nodes-only/--edges-only for scoping. The ORCHESTRATOR declares the real rhythm (cse_producers_nightly :13, :19-20): 'the first graph_head fire IS the ~55k backfill; every later fire appends only the graph delta', with CSE_GRAPHHEAD_ENABLED defaulting to 1 and the leg running 'build_graph_head_cses at FULL scope behind the dedup filter'.
cadence.actual_trigger: THE NIGHTLY TASK, THROUGH leg_graphhead -- NOT THROUGH THIS MODULE'S main(). leg_graphhead (:146-160) imports the module, calls build_graph_head_cses(catalog, marker, limit=None, nodes_only=False, edges_only=False) -- full scope -- then applies filter_new(built, existing) to drop event_ids already in the table before validating and appending. main() is never on that path, and it is the ONLY path with a different dedup story (see failure_mode). CSE_GRAPHHEAD_ENABLED defaults to 1, and the module's own self-test asserts the posture graph_head=ON, sweep=ON, agent=OFF (:387-388).
cadence.live_instance_age: CURRENT -- the newest partition is event_date 2026-08-30. But the calendar is not complete: 44 partitions across a 54-calendar-day span (2026-07-08..2026-08-30) leaves 10 DAYS WITH NO PARTITION AT ALL -- a contiguous seven-day gap 2026-07-09..2026-07-15 immediately after the first fire, then isolated misses on 07-26, 08-03 and 08-10. A partition is absent when the leg produced no new event_ids OR when it did not run, and the two are the same observable from the table; I did not measure which, and I am not inferring it. I first typed 'partial' into live_matches_declared, which is not a member of the declared enum ['yes','no','unmeasured','not_applicable'] -- inventing a value rather than choosing one is the taxonomy failure the schema exists to refuse, and the gate caught it. The correct member is 'yes': the orchestrator declares delta-only appends after the first backfill, and a day with no new event_ids therefore PREDICTS an absent partition -- so the 10 gaps are CONSISTENT WITH the declaration, not evidence against it. What I have not measured is whether the leg also failed to run on any of those days; that alternative is not excluded.

coverage.universe: Every row of graph_nodes and every row of graph_edges visible to the catalog at emission, less unmapped edge_types, less event_ids already present in the table.
coverage.denominator: THIS PRODUCER PRINTS ITS DENOMINATORS, AND THAT IS A REAL CREDIT ON A FACE WHERE THE OTHER SUBJECTS DO NOT. The node line prints 'recognized=N (of {len(nodes)} live nodes)' (:169) and the edge line prints 'recognized=N skipped_unmapped_edge_type=M (of {len(edges)} live edges)' (:184-186) -- so the skipped edges are COUNTED and surfaced, not dropped silently, which is exactly what cse_emit_deploy fails to do at its own drop site. The orchestrator adds built / skipped_existing to its summary (:151). WHAT IS STILL NOT VISIBLE: a node whose map_cloudnode lookup misses is not counted anywhere -- it is emitted as Concept+0.2 rather than skipped, so the untyped share is recoverable only by reading the table, and it is 32,419 of 86,607 rows (37%).

key.identity_space: CSE event ids in the GRAPH_HEAD namespace, keyed on the GRAPH's identity space rather than on the run: a node id, or a (src, edge_type, dst) triple. The producer ref is the Nessie marker, so producer identity is run-scoped while event identity is not.
key.key_expression: NODE: f'graph_head:node:{nid}' (:107). EDGE: f'graph_head:edge:{src}->{edge_type}->{dst}' (:141). No truncation on either. THE OMISSION OF THE MARKER FROM THE EVENT ID IS THE DESIGN, NOT A DEFECT -- it is precisely what lets filter_new turn a full re-scan into a delta, and it is why 44 nightly full-scope runs produced 86,607 rows instead of millions. I had it the other way round in draft and the measurement corrected me: ZERO event_ids appear on more than one day, across all 44 partitions.
key.declared_mapping: The orchestrator declares the dedup contract explicitly (:19-20, 'at FULL scope behind the dedup filter (event_ids graph_head:node:{nid} / graph_head:edge:{...})'), so the key expression is named in the place that depends on it. NOT DECLARED: that the (src, edge_type, dst) triple is not unique in graph_edges -- see the exercised duplicate in failure_mode.
key.evidence: Key expressions at :107 and :141; the orchestrator's declaration at :19-20. Cross-run uniqueness measured over all 44 partitions: 86,600 distinct event_ids over 86,607 rows, with 0 event_ids appearing on more than one day.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: ONE HANDLER IN THE MODULE, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. An AST census (attribution-controlled) finds exactly one except-handler: _current_marker :66, `except Exception` -> print WARN, return the literal string 'unknown'. Every other failure propagates -- _scan does not guard load_table or scan, and build_graph_head_cses does not guard the loops. THE SAME MODULE CONTAINS AN EXPLICITLY DOCUMENTED FAIL-LOUD CONTRACT TWO FUNCTIONS LOWER: distinct_raw_edge_types (:87-91) states 'FAIL-LOUD (spec Sec 1, THE load-bearing guard): a get_catalog / load_table / scan error PROPAGATES here (this NEVER returns a silent empty on error)'. So the module demonstrably knows the failure-philosophy question, argues it at length for the edge-type inventory, and answers it the other way for the marker -- without saying so.
silent_degrade_paths: 'unknown' HAS TWO CAUSES AND ONLY ONE OF THEM PRINTS. The except arm at :66 prints WARN: NESSIE_HEAD_FAIL. But the success arm at :65 is `data.get('hash') or (data.get('reference') or {}).get('hash') or 'unknown'` -- a 200 response whose payload carries neither field yields the identical 'unknown' with NO output at all. A reader who greps the logs for NESSIE_HEAD_FAIL would see nothing and conclude the marker was read. MEASURED: this has NEVER fired -- 0 of 86,607 rows carry 'unknown', all 44 marker_head values are distinct 64-character hashes, exactly one per partition. It is a latent hazard with a real blast radius (four fields), not a live defect, and the card says so

THE MODULE'S OWN main() HAS NO DEDUP OF ANY KIND, AND THE ONE PARTITION IT PRODUCED CARRIES THE FINGERPRINT. main() calls cse_store.append_cses directly (:219), and append_cses does NOT filter by event_id -- it validates and appends every row it is given (cse_store.py:357-393, read in full). The only dedup in the system is filter_new, which lives in the orchestrator (:116) and collapses in-batch duplicates as well as dropping existing ones (asserted by its own self-test at :374-375). EXERCISED: the 2026-07-08 partition is 50 rows = 25 nodes + 25 edges, which is exactly this module's default limit of 25 (:199) and therefore a main() run -- and it holds only 43 distinct event_ids, because ONE edge id (an instance-profile ASSUMES edge) appears EIGHT times with an identical ingested_at. Every other partition has zero duplicates. So the (src, edge_type, dst) triple is not unique in graph_edges, this module cannot see that, and production is protected only because the orchestrator dedups on its behalf

A CHANGED OR DELETED GRAPH OBJECT NEVER UPDATES ITS CSE. verb is create for 86,607 of 86,607 rows and the event_id carries no marker and no content hash, so once a node id is in the table filter_new suppresses it forever -- including after its node_type, and therefore its Entity mapping and confidence, has changed. A deleted node's CSE also stands. Reconstructing state from source=graph_head therefore yields the UNION of everything ever seen, not the graph's HEAD. The log is append-only by design and the docstring says 'verb=create per the HEAD state', so this is a consequence of a stated design rather than a violation of it -- but the name 'graph_head' invites the other reading, and nothing in the stream distinguishes a live node from one deleted in July
a --nodes-only or --edges-only run still prints only the line for the grain it ran, so a scoped run and a run whose other grain produced nothing look alike in the log
execution_meta.actor is the hardcoded '0.5.0_AE_OpalETL' (:117, :148) regardless of who ran it -- the same trap as the deploy producer, and exercised the same way: every row carries that actor

AN OWNED_BY EDGE WITH AN UNKNOWN OBJECT TYPE SILENTLY DEFAULTS TO OWNS, AND THE CENSUS BUILT TO CATCH THAT IS NEVER CALLED HERE. cse_schema.map_cloudedge (:399-403) resolves OWNED_BY to CONTAINS when the destination type is in _OWNED_BY_CONTAINER_TYPES and to OWNS otherwise -- and cse_schema's own owned_by_object_census (:406-413) states that an object type in NEITHER the actor nor the container set 'currently DEFAULTS to OWNS via map_cloudedge -- which is WRONG for a new CONTAINER', and exists to 'Surface it for a governed whitelist-bump ... NEVER silently default'. This producer calls map_cloudedge on every edge and NEVER calls owned_by_object_census, so on this path a new container type is absorbed as custody with confidence 1.0 and nothing prints. The hazard is DECLARED by the mapping module and UNGUARDED by this consumer; whether any live OWNED_BY object type is currently unknown is NOT measured here -- that census is the remedy, and running it is not this card's act.

verdict.why: This is the strongest of the three producers carded so far and the card should be specific about why: it is one of the TWO live producers on this face (44 partitions, 86,607 rows, current to today) and the larger of them -- I first wrote 'the only one', which my credit census falsified against my own card-1 measurement: source=agent is equally current at 43 partitions, it PRINTS ITS DENOMINATORS at both grains including the count of edges it skipped, it refuses to invent a relationship for an unmapped edge_type, it resolves OWNED_BY by the destination node type rather than with a flat lookup that could not disambiguate -- and I verified that in cse_schema.map_cloudedge (:399-403), not from the call site's comment about it, because a credit resting on an unread dependency is the class this face keeps catching, and it carries an explicitly argued FAIL-LOUD contract on its edge-type inventory. QUALIFIED on four measured points. FIRST, the production path is leg_graphhead, not this module's main() -- the same class this face's card 1 found in the agent producer, and here it has a visible fingerprint: main() has no dedup at all, append_cses does not dedup either, and the single partition main() produced carries one edge event_id eight times while all 43 other partitions are clean. Production is correct only because the orchestrator deduplicates on the module's behalf. SECOND, _current_marker fails soft to the literal 'unknown' and that value would reach four fields -- and it has TWO causes of which only one prints, so the silent cause would be invisible to a log search. It has never fired in 86,607 rows, which is why this is recorded as a latent hazard and not a defect. THIRD, the stream cannot express change or deletion: every row is create, the event_id is keyed on graph identity alone, so a node that changes type keeps its first CSE and a deleted node keeps its CSE forever. FOURTH, the calendar has 10 missing days in a 54-day span including a contiguous seven-day gap, and an absent partition does not distinguish 'no new event_ids' from 'did not run'. Two of my own errors are recorded rather than only the subject's: I drafted the event_id omission as a defect when it is the mechanism that makes the delta work, and I hypothesised store-side dedup before reading append_cses, which does not dedup. Both were corrected by measurement before this card was written.
